step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Primary subject of case report: 81-year-old female presenting with severe COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP)

evidence_items.source_quote: She had been tested for COVID-19 before admission to the hospital, and a positive polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test was reported.
After admission to Khorshid Hospital, another PCR test was performed to confirm the previous findings, and it was positive again for COVID-19.

A ground-glass pattern was reported in the high-resolution computed tomography (CT) of the lung. Spiral multislices showed diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacity and crazy paving opacity with peripheral and peribronchovascular distribution, a pattern highly suggestive of COVID-19-associated pneumonia [Figure 1].

rationale: An 81-year-old female presented with fever, cough, dyspnea, and loss of consciousness. She had two positive PCR tests for COVID-19 (before and after hospital admission), providing E1 confirmatory lab evidence. High-resolution chest CT showed bilateral ground-glass and crazy paving opacities typical of COVID-19 pneumonia. Assertion CONFIRMED_PRESENT, temporality CURRENT_EPISODE, clinical role PRIMARY_DIAGNOSIS. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.
